newsitem.title: UK: Scottish poll shows slight rise in Tory support.
newsitem.headline: Scottish poll shows slight rise in Tory support.

text.p: Support for Britain's ruling Conservatives rose one point in the latest Scottish opinion poll but the party is still third-placed in Scotland at less than half its 1992 general election support.
The monthly System Three poll puts Prime Minister John Major's party on 12 per cent and Tony Blair's opposition Labour dropping back two points to 53 percent in voter support.
The survey of voting intentions published in the Herald newspaper on Tuesday shows the pro-independence Scottish National Party (SNP) remaining in second place and up one point to 24 percent.
Liberal Democrats gained two points to 10.
The poll was carried out before last week's budget in 40 of Scotland's 72 parliamentary seats.
A general election must be held by May 1997. Conservatives at present have 10 Scottish M.P.s., Labour 49, Liberal Democrats 9, and SNP four.
